Difficile d’obtenir un travail qualifié: Skilled Jobs Hard to Come By for Asylum Seekers
La recherche d’emploi peut être un parco: Job hunting can be an obstacle course, but for asylum seekers, it comes with its share of frustrations.
Mamadou, un demandeur d’asile sénégalais: Mamadou, a Senegalese asylum seeker, shares his experience, which is similar to that of many others. Credit: Anaïs Elboujdaïni
Au Québec, la recherche d’emploi peut êt: In Quebec, job hunting can be an obstacle course, but for asylum seekers, it comes with its share of frustrations, especially for those whose professional qualifications are not recognized. Mamadou, a Senegalese asylum seeker, shares his experience, which is similar to that of many others.
La lumière d’hiver filtre par les vastes: Winter light filters through the large bay windows of the Grande Bibliothèque in Montréal.
Mamadou s’y rend souvent. Il y passe ses: Mamadou often comes here. He spends his days doing research. His expertise in human rights advocacy, acquired notably with the UN in Senegal, has not opened the doors of the Quebec job market. “I have experience, but nobody wants it,” he laments.
Ayant également des compétences en prote: He also has skills in environmental protection, and he remembers a trip that took him and other Senegalese advocates to Poland. There, they saw that coal-fired power plants had been shut down and converted into office complexes.
« Il y a une petite ville qui s’appelle: “There's a small town called Bargny, where the Senegalese state opened a coal-fired power plant, and it led to a conflict between the residents of Bargny and the government in power,” he says.
Malgré ces expériences internationales d: Despite this international experience fighting climate change and monitoring discharges hazardous to local populations in Senegal, last summer in Quebec he was only able to land a position intended for people with no experience. It is a job at a non-profit organization whose name he prefers not to give.
Rapidement, ses collègues, de jeunes cég: Soon, his colleagues, young CEGEP and university students in summer jobs, told him they didn't understand why, with his experience, he wasn't at least their supervisor.
« Mais quand on arrive, on sent qu’il y: “But when you arrive, you feel there is a certain professional stigma. Because you arrive here, and they let you know indirectly that we do not recognize your diplomas,” Mamadou recounts.
« Aucun demandeur d’asile qui arrive n’a: “No asylum seeker who arrives has the goal of holding out a hand and receiving welfare. Every one of them wants a professional life,” he insists. “But how do you explain that Quebec, which says it needs labour, makes employment programs inaccessible, at least for asylum seekers?” Mamadou asks.
Mamadou est actif sur une page Facebook: Mamadou is active on a Facebook page for asylum seekers. He is often the first to offer precise, well-researched advice in response to the questions posted there. How do I get welfare? How do I stop receiving it if I have a job? Where can I find a good lawyer? If my roommate has a criminal record, could it affect my own asylum claim? These are questions that a caring, multicultural community does its best to answer with what it knows. Mamadou says community workers sometimes write to him privately to ask for advice.
C’est grâce à ses recherches quotidienne: It is thanks to his daily research at the Grande Bibliothèque that he can answer his fellow asylum seekers. “That's how I discovered that we didn't have access to certain employability programs,” he says.
Le ministère de l’Emploi du Québec le co: Quebec's Ministry of Employment confirms it: “Asylum seekers are, however, ineligible for the active employment measures of the Ministère de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale.” This situation leaves a large number of people in limbo, unable to put their skills and professional experience to use.
Le porte-parole du ministère nuance cepe: The ministry's spokesperson adds some nuance, however: “An asylum seeker can go to a Services Québec office and benefit from universal employment services such as access to online placement services, labour market information and group sessions.” These services cover the job market, the résumé and the cover letter.
Par ailleurs, le ministère de l’Emploi a: In addition, the Ministry of Employment recently announced two pilot projects aimed at helping asylum seekers who hold a work permit and are interested in the tourism sector or the health and social services field. The goal? To allow more people to join programs they previously could not access.
Simon, un demandeur d’asile, est un exem: Is Simon, an asylum seeker, an example of this exclusion from job integration programs? He was in fact refused a position in a social integration program because of his immigration status.
Dans un courriel qu’a pu consulter La Co: In an email seen by La Converse, the program manager at a Montréal organization replied to him as follows: “Unfortunately, your status as an asylum seeker does not make you eligible to participate. If your status changes to accepted refugee (protected person), you will then be eligible for our program.”
« C’est frustrant », lâche Simon, qui a: “It's frustrating,” Simon says, who has received this type of message several times.
De son côté, le Centre social d’aide aux: For its part, the Centre social d'aide aux immigrants has an officer dedicated to job searching for asylum seekers. However, the people in charge of the employment program declined our interview request.
D’autres centres qui offrent des service: Other centres that offer similar services did not respond to our interview requests.

Cette année, El Niño a rendu l’hiver plu: This year, El Niño made the winter milder than usual. The weather nonetheless decided to give us a real winter day last December, on the day of the second asylum seekers' job fair.
Dès l’ouverture du Salon, une longue fil: As soon as the fair opens, a long line forms outside, under the snowflakes.
Manuel*, un Colombien établi au Québec d: Manuel*, a Colombian who has lived in Quebec for four years, has just finished his French-language integration course. He is surprised by the number of people at the fair. “I waited almost an hour to get in,” he says, standing slightly apart from a group of job seekers.
Plusieurs organismes sont présents pour: Several organizations are on hand to inform asylum seekers of their rights and tell them, for example, that employment insurance is theirs if they lose a job. Other organizations provide information on finding housing.
Samira*, demandeuse d’asile d’Ouganda, e: Samira*, an asylum seeker from Uganda, has been in Canada for three months when we meet her. She is especially surprised by the number of resources that exist and that she had never heard of. An English speaker, she believes English is a barrier to accessing certain services.
« Je suis contente d’être venue ici aujo: “I'm glad I came here today because I learned that we have access to help with housing,” says the woman, who was a housekeeper in her country of origin.
Des agences de placement sont aussi là,: Placement agencies are there too, along with employers, though fewer of them. One is Excavation HEBR, a company founded by Alexandre Hébert. Specializing in excavation, the young entrepreneur from the Montréal area is generating some excitement at the fair.
« Je pense que c’est grâce à notre gros: “I think it's thanks to our big toy,” he exclaims, all smiles, pointing at a scaled-down excavator that is still big enough to draw attention. The toy, a replica of a real construction machine, instantly sparks conversations with the men, who rush to hand him their résumés.
« On recherche une plus longue relation: “We're looking for a longer relationship with our workers. Sometimes, hiring temporary foreign workers means they don't necessarily come back – there's quite a lot of turnover and the training is lost. Whereas here, our initiative is more about keeping a relationship with INICI, and then building a long-term relationship with our workers [who are asylum seekers],” Mr. Hébert explains with conviction. INICI's mission is to offer personalized integration, French-language learning and employment assistance services to immigrants.
Alexandre Hébert a fait le pari d’embauc: Alexandre Hébert has bet on hiring asylum seekers. He loves it when they already have construction training from their country of origin because he considers it a golden opportunity to exchange knowledge. Photo: Anais ElboujdaÏni
Ce que M. Hébert adore également, c’est: Mr. Hébert also loves to pick asylum seekers who have construction training in their country of origin so he can compare methods once on the job site. “It's always very enriching,” he confirms.
Depuis quelques mois, les travailleurs é: For the past few months, temporary foreign workers have been at the heart of debates about Quebec's and Canada's capacity to take in newcomers.
Ottawa a d’ailleurs durci le ton : à par: Ottawa has also taken a harder line: starting May 1<sup>st</sup>, 2024, access to the Temporary Foreign Worker Program (TFWP) will be reduced. The number of temporary foreign workers that businesses can hire will be capped at 20% of their staff (except in health care and construction).
Mo, demandeur d’asile de Djibouti qui a: Mo, an asylum seeker from Djibouti who left his country because of political persecution, trained as a banker. “I'm not here for fun,” he says.
Son regard amusé exprime néanmoins une c: His amused look nonetheless conveys a certain resignation. He knows he won't be working as a banker. So his dream is at least to work, and to like what he does a little. “You need Quebec experience; I don't think it will be easy for me to get a position I aspire to. We'll see if I can get one of the positions I aspire to, but I'll apply for any job.”
Lui qui avait l’habitude de subvenir aux: Having been used to providing for his family, he wants to be financially independent again. “Right now, friends are putting me up because welfare isn't enough,” says Mo, who has been waiting for his work permit since August 2023.
Mamadou s’étonne que ses compétences ne: Mamadou is surprised that his skills are not recognized.
« En tant que demandeur d’asile, vous de: “As an asylum seeker, you have to make even more effort to reach the same professional level. You have a bachelor's degree, but as an asylum seeker, you have to work even harder to prove yourself. You get the feeling that the professional experience we gained abroad is underestimated here,” he says.
Il ne s’attendait pas à un tel défi, car:
He didn't expect such a challenge, because “the message Canada puts out abroad is a flattering one that says, ‘We need labour.’” Entire networks of influencers, in Africa in particular, tout an idyllic way of life in Canada, <l1>which explains the disappointment once people arrive, as a journalist from Zimbabwe reports</l1>.

Like many others, Mamadou hopes the doors can open wider to include those who may be Canadian citizens tomorrow.
« Avec un peu d’effort, avec une bonne p: “With a little effort, with good policy, I think Canada can succeed in integrating asylum seekers,” Mamadou declares.
Il se demande toutefois s’il a fait le b: He wonders, however, whether he made the right choice, because today he is still waiting for his hearing to be heard as a refugee. Imprisoned several times in Senegal, he fled persecution.
« Donc sur le plan mental, peut-être que: “So mentally, maybe you fled prison in your country, but now, [Canada has my passport] and I feel a bit condemned to wait, because we know nothing about hearing dates.”
